newsitem.title: USA: Clinton admits taking 'gratuity' -- an $18 watch. [CORRECTED 21:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Clinton admits taking 'gratuity' -- an $18 watch. [CORRECTED 21:55 GMT]

text.p: President Bill Clinton came clean on Monday about accepting a "gratuity" at a meeting of educational leaders: he admitted taking an $18 watch offered by the chancellor of the California State University (Corrects from University of California).

"Since we're in the spirit of full disclosure, I have to tell you that in addition to my coming here today, I received a gratuity, which I intend to disclose before the whole world," Clinton told the American Council of Education, a group of college and university administrators.

"I complimented Barry (Munitz, head of the council and of the California State University system) on his watch, and he gave it to me," Clinton said to general laughter and applause. "And cravenly, as we politicians are, I took it without blinking. He swears it cost $18."
Munitz, who sat on the dais behind Clinton, raised both hands to show that his wrists were bare.
Clinton said he liked the new watch because of its large numbers.
"It's the first watch I've ever seen I don't need glasses for," he said.

Clinton made note of the current furore over campaign financing, saying: "You know, we're all in a lather up here in Washington these days about campaign contributions; everybody hates them, but nobody wants to go to public funding. So we seem destined to some period of hand-wringing."
